note: Which Clients views EXIST for anybody (comma-separated: directory, record, unique). A view removed here disappears for every user — the sidebar, the chooser and deep links all refuse it. The per-user Views button can only hide what this allows.

Which toolbar buttons exist on the Clients selection screens, comma-separated: share, export, add. Remove one and it disappears for everyone. Views is not listed because it is ALWAYS available — it is how people reach the views at all. (Legacy values: yes = all three, no = none.)

Which Hiring views EXIST for anybody (comma-separated: pipeline, table, calendar, actions, documents, reports, analysis, scores). A view removed here disappears for every user — the chooser and the deep links refuse it. The word flow still stands for the views the old Flow rail held (table, calendar, actions, documents, reports), so this shipped value keeps meaning what it meant. The Board left that list on 2026-08-27 — it drew the same rows the Pipeline draws — so a cell that still names it simply loses that word. The Archive is not a view and is not governed here.

Anyone signed in may send e-mail AS the platform (asa-hub@asaop.org) from the e-mail icon. Set to no to switch the composer off for everyone at once. The inbox view is unaffected: that is the master's alone.

Which BADGES read the platform mailbox in the Mail app (comma-separated from the official type vocabulary, e.g. DIRECTOR, ADMINISTRATOR). The master always reads it; everyone else gets the same 404 as before — the box is never advertised. A cell naming one badge also admits any badge currently equivalent to it (Profile.gs HUB_BADGE_FOLLOWS) — name that badge here to keep it once they part.
How often the contact clock runs (phones fill + Quo enrich), in hours. Allowed: 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12 — anything else falls back to 2. Saving from Settings reinstalls the trigger with the new cadence.
Which Potential Clients views EXIST for anybody (comma-separated: pipeline, unique). A view removed here disappears for every user — the same law the Clients and Hiring views obey.

SMS goes to these numbers (comma-separated, +1XXXXXXXXXX). This row ADDS to the escalation floor below and cannot shorten it — to change who is always paged, edit the floor itself. 4040 is deliberately absent: the phone-screen line stays free.

Who is ALWAYS paged by an escalation, whatever else is configured (comma-separated, +1XXXXXXXXXX). Every other recipient list adds to this one. Emptying this row does NOT turn escalations off — it restores the shipped numbers. Put a different person here to change who is paged. Never add 3307544040: that is the phone-screen line and it stays free.

Messages that mean "stop texting me" (comma-separated). The whole message must match one of them. Empty = the shipped list: stop, stopall, unsubscribe, cancel, end, quit, revoke, optout, opt out, remove me, pare, parar, para, nao quero, não quero, remova, descadastrar, sair. ANYTHING TYPED HERE REPLACES that list — it does not add to it. Type "cancelar" alone and stop and pare stop being heard, on every channel, from the next message on. To add a word, type the shipped ones again beside it.

Messages that mean "you can text me again" (comma-separated). Empty = the shipped list: start, unstop, resume, voltar, pode mandar. "yes" is deliberately NOT on it: of 89 messages it would have matched, 88 were somebody answering a question and one was a real start — and an opt-in RELEASES a suppression, so that list would have un-silenced people who never asked to be. ANYTHING TYPED HERE REPLACES the shipped list — it does not add to it.

Messages that mean "you have the wrong person" (comma-separated). The whole message must match one of them — "I called the wrong number earlier" is somebody explaining, not somebody telling us to stop. Suppressed like a stop, but recorded as its own reason: the number is bad data of OURS, not a decision of theirs. Empty = the shipped list: wrong number, wrong person, you have the wrong number, sorry wrong number, this is not me, not me, numero errado, número errado, nao sou eu, não sou eu, pessoa errada. ANYTHING TYPED HERE REPLACES that list — it does not add to it.

THE ONE SWITCH. on (also: sheet, rehearsal, paper) = NOTHING LEAVES the platform, on any channel, to anybody — testers included: every message is written as a row in the mock outbox (comm_mock) and the rehearsal house, and the sending dial follows it (record). It is the emergency stop: turning it on is never refused. off = normal operation, real recipients, and the sending dial follows it (send) with no second step. The only letters that still leave while it is on are the two a person just asked for — a password reset and an invitation to register. Empty means it has never been set, and is read as ON while a tester is listed — so upgrading the code can never silently point a message at real people.

The testers' numbers (+1XXXXXXXXXX, comma-separated). Nothing is redirected to them any more — test mode on sends nothing to anybody — so this list only names who the testers are, for the screens that show it.
The same for e-mail — one or several addresses, comma-separated. Nothing is redirected here either; test mode on sends nothing to anybody.

Where a TEST card's New Hire packet request is sent instead of to the card's own number (+1XXXXXXXXXX). A card is a rehearsal when its name starts "[test]", or it carries the rehearsal line or e-mail. EMPTY = rehearsals are logged and nothing is sent, which is the safe default; fill this in to prove the lane really delivers. A rehearsal never reaches the person on the card and never pages the team.
Badges that keep the Copilot star (top bar + command bar). Empty = everyone. Edited from Settings - Access control - Features.
Badges that get the My world card (a personal world of their own). A world is everyone's own ground: EMPTY = everybody has one. Naming badges NARROWS it. The MASTER always has it.
Badges that see the Smart Comms indicator ("Your notifications") on My asa. — the platform's send activity, which is an admin's view rather than a caregiver's. Empty = everyone.
Badges that see the franchise card(s) in the places stack (e.g. DIRECTOR). The MASTER always sees them; empty = the master alone.
Badges that keep the four-squares App Hub button on the command bar. Empty = everyone.

Badges that read EVERYBODY's Behavior Support — the wellbeing reading of how people work here. The rule: it is visible down to the house manager's badge, and every badge below that reads only its own. Everyone else opens the app and sees THEIR OWN reading and nobody else's — the app is never closed to a person about themselves. The MASTER always reads everybody; EMPTY = the master alone (fail closed, because these rows are about named people).

Badges that may EDIT in Render Sheet — change cells and add rows (comma-separated). Empty = admins only. Everyone the app matrix admits may still VIEW. Edited from Settings - Access control - Features.
Email goes to these addresses (comma-separated). Arthur Torres · Ty Bond · Asatech. Arthur reads admin@abrighterdawninc.com, not arthur.torres@.

WHO IS ASKED to decide in the hiring pipeline (comma-separated): the shortlist, the phone-screen decision, the CJIS request and the discard notice all go here. Arthur Torres · Ty Bond · Wellington (admin@abrighterdawninc.com). Empty falls back to the staff alert recipients, so it degrades to "the usual people" and never to nobody. Display names come from the users tab at runtime — nothing here is a name.

WHO confirms in-person interviews — the Division Supervisor, named by the display name on her users row. Her phone and e-mail are read from that row at runtime, so keep the row current (her number has historically been +13303440430). You may append a number after the name ("Name, +1XXXXXXXXXX") to override the phone without touching her row. Change the name here and the interview loop texts somebody else tomorrow.

default_value: Your signed New Hire packet — ASA Lifecare

Hi DSP,

To finish your onboarding we still need your signed New Hire packet.

note: (moved to Smart Comms 2026-08-17 — hiring_packet_request; history.) Body of the same request by e-mail. Placeholders: {name}

Optional line put at the TOP of every redirected message while test mode is on, saying who it would really have gone to — {to} is that person. EMPTY by default because it lands inside the message a tester reads, and a rehearsal is worth more when it looks exactly like the real thing. While it is empty the real destination is still recorded in System logs, and e-mails still carry [TEST] in the SUBJECT.

WHO MAY SIGN AN INTERVIEW SCORECARD, besides the interviewer login itself. Comma-separated e-mail addresses. Empty = only the interviewer account. The scorecard is an attestation that somebody sat in a room with the candidate, so this list is short on purpose — an admin is NOT admitted by being an admin. Edit it here or straight in the hiring_alerts_config tab; it is the same cell, and removing an address revokes immediately on that person's next request.

The timezone the hiring lane counts days in. Blank = America/New_York. The project manifest is also America/New_York (flipped 2026-08-15); this override exists from the Sao_Paulo era, when every "start of day" landed at 19:00 the previous evening in Ohio. Leave it blank unless the company moves.

The candidate's day to produce the signed packet. Blank = 24 hours. It no longer decides the colour — the card is amber the moment onboarding ends — only WHEN THE SECOND message goes out saying the day ran out. Hours, whole numbers.

How many days BEFORE their onboarding date a new hire may start the portal. Blank = 1. Anchored on onboarding_scheduled_for, which is stamped when the card reaches Onboarding. A card with no date is ALWAYS open — nothing to anchor to must never mean nobody gets in.

How many days AFTER their onboarding date the portal stays open. Blank = 7, deliberately longer than the interview's: a visit that gets interrupted is normally resumed within the week, and the cost of this being too tight is a real new hire locked out of the one screen that lets them finish.

on = the SEND DOOR hands nothing over — an EXTRA brake, not the emergency stop: the team notices, the platform mailbox's direct letters and the hiring simulator do not pass that door. To stop everything, turn test_mode on. It can only narrow: it cannot switch sending ON, because that stays with HUB_RPC_SEND in Script Properties where a spreadsheet cannot reach it. Blank or off = normal.
(moved to Smart Comms 2026-08-17 — the hiring_date_accepted situation governs; this row is history.) Date Accepted could not be read. Placeholders: {name} {phone} {email} {screen} {report}
(moved to Smart Comms 2026-08-17 — hiring_hired_complete; history.) Hired with everything green. Placeholders: {name} {phone} {email} {manual_note}
(moved to Smart Comms 2026-08-17 — hiring_hired_missing; history.) Hired with items missing. Placeholders: {name} {phone} {email} {missing}

Signed-in lanes (add candidate, resume intake, edit contact). shadow = allow and log only; enforce = refuse. Keep it on shadow until the override modal exists — the refusal text offers an admin/manager override that no screen can send yet, so enforcing is a wall with no door.

The PUBLIC referral form. Starts as shadow on purpose: a refusal there is invisible to the sender, so a false positive silently loses a real referral. Watch referral_staff_conflict in the logs before setting enforce.

Which people.status values mean SOMEBODY WORKS HERE NOW. Allowlist, never a denylist: the column is free text and already holds "active test" and one cell reading "employee status: yes". TWO THINGS DEPEND ON IT, and the second arrived on 2026-08-28. (1) A matching status REFUSES a card in the contact guard; everything else only warns. (2) It decides whether somebody crossing in from the Talent Pipeline is treated as STAFF — landing at Ready to start with the record closing itself minutes later — or as a CANDIDATE who walks the whole process. Widen this list and a returning employee stops being hired; narrow it and a current one gets a hiring process they do not need.
Numbers that are always a rehearsal and never collide; the 5558 is the one that behaves differently. Company lines are exempt separately.
Addresses that never collide. One trailing wildcard allowed. Exempts the EMAIL axis only — a test address never excuses a real phone number.
Institutional mailboxes: they identify nobody, like a company phone line, so they never count as a match.

Settings > My Work, set by the master account alone. yes hides the black header of My Work (the four figures and the line under them) from every account except the master's own session. Anything but yes reads as no.

Settings > My Work, set by the master account alone. yes hides the grey and amber note lines under the card titles of My Work from every account except the master's own session. A source that could not be read is still said.
Settings > My Work, set by the master account alone. yes leaves the folded Nothing on file for N requirements row off My Work for every account except the master's own session.

Settings > My Work, set by the master account alone. yes leaves every concluded request off My Work for every account except the master's own session: anything resolved (covered, closed, approved, denied, past), and any late call, call-off or incident report about a day before today. One about today or a later day stays. The relay never sends those rows, and Show resolved disappears.

Settings > My Work, set by the master account alone. yes hides the Sources card of My Inbox (where each alert comes from, what each source could tell, and what is not on the platform yet) from every account except the master's own session. The relay never sends that list; the alerts, the unread counts and the empty sentence stay.

Settings > My Work, set by the master account alone. yes hides every Updated … ago and Read … freshness stamp (Locations, Clients, Staff, SSA, Families, Staff Candidates, Client Candidates, My Work, My Profile, My Calendar, My Inbox) from every account except the master's own session; it rides the session (authMe, authLogin stamps_hidden). The key keeps its old name so the saved value carries over. Ships as yes; anything but yes reads as no.

Settings > My Work, set by the master account alone. yes shows the agency alone in the SSA app's COUNTY / AGENCY line (Stark County Board of DD, never FRAN County · Stark County Board of DD) for every account except the master's own session. Ships as yes.

Settings > My Work, set by the master account alone. yes hides the count line under Associated clients in the SSA app (1 client whose record names this SSA.) from every account except the master's own session. The clients stay listed. Ships as yes.

Settings > My Work, set by the master account alone. yes leaves the role (Service and Support Administrator) off each associated client in the SSA app, so the line shows the house alone, for every account except the master's own session. Ships as yes.

Settings > My Work, set by the master account alone. yes hides the hours column (Hrs (week) / Hrs (tab) and its On shift total) in Scheduling from every account except the master's own session; staff see the role badges instead. An unreadable setting hides. Ships as yes; anything but yes reads as no.

Settings > My Work, set by the master account alone. yes hides the grey source notes under a Staff section (a missing source column or a source that could not answer, such as the Employee Database Master has no column for sam, oig) from every account except the master's own session; it rides the session (authMe, authLogin record_notes_hidden). The Part of this could not be read warning stays. An unreadable setting hides. Ships as yes; anything but yes reads as no.

Settings > My Work, set by the master account alone. Comma-separated app ids that only the master's own session sees: every other account is handed App Control without them, as if they were never released. Empty shows every app as App Control has it; an unreadable setting cuts nothing.

Settings > My Work, set by the master account alone. Comma-separated account ids (USR_) that see the apps on mywork_hide_apps too, each as App Control has it; they are never told the list exists. Empty lets nobody but the master in; an unreadable setting lets nobody in.

Settings > My Work, set by the master account alone. yes keeps My World to the master's own session and the accounts on mywork_hide_world_seen: every other account is answered as one Worlds are not offered to (no place, no door, no Settings tab), and nothing of theirs is deleted. Ships as no; anything but yes, or an unreadable setting, reads as no.

Settings > My Work, set by the master account alone. Comma-separated account ids (USR_) that keep their world while mywork_hide_world is yes; they are never told the list exists. Empty lets nobody but the master in; an unreadable setting lets nobody in.

Settings > My Work, set by the master account alone. yes keeps My asa. and Bookmarks to the master's own session and the accounts on mywork_hide_myasa_seen: every other account is answered as one they were never offered to (no app, no route, no bookmark toggle), and nobody's saved bookmarks are deleted. Ships as no; anything but yes, or an unreadable setting, reads as no.

Settings > My Work, set by the master account alone. Comma-separated account ids (USR_) that keep My asa. and their Bookmarks while mywork_hide_myasa is yes; they are never told the list exists. Empty lets nobody but the master in; an unreadable setting lets nobody in.

Settings > App Control access, set by the master account alone. The accounts App Control is shared with, as a list: for each account (USR_ id), the exact apps it sees inside App Control and whether it may change them. A delegate sees those apps' rows and the controls inside them, nothing else, and with May change off only views. Empty shares App Control with nobody; an unreadable setting shares it with nobody.

Settings > Editions, set by the master account alone. The delicate edits each app offers, as a list: for each edition (an id such as locations.house), whether its key is on and the accounts (USR_ ids) that may make it. The master makes every edition, always; anybody else only while its key is on and they are on its list. Empty, or an unreadable setting, gives nobody but the master any edition.

Settings > My Work > Support Requests, set by the master account alone. ON means a Late Show becomes a warning request "Directors, are you aware?" in Support Requests plus a red My Inbox item for each director; no text (Smart Comms staff_late_show already speaks). Ships off; unreadable reads off.

Settings > My Work > Support Requests, set by the master account alone. ON means a No Call No Show becomes a warning request "Directors, are you aware?" in Support Requests plus a red My Inbox item for each director; no text (Smart Comms staff_no_call already speaks). Ships off; unreadable reads off.

Settings > My Work > Support Requests, set by the master account alone. ON means the first missing clock-in or clock-out per person per shift becomes a warning request and a red My Inbox item for the directors and the leads, then a text through the Smart Comms situation sr_punch_aware. Ships off; unreadable reads off.

Settings > My Work > Support Requests, set by the master account alone. ON means every incident filed (hotline, platform form, the estate's form) becomes an important alert for the directors and the leads: a pointer (category, location, day), never the report. Ships off; unreadable reads off.

Settings > My Work > Support Requests, set by the master account alone. ON means an Other - General Requests row gets a My Inbox item for each lead; no second text (hotline_support_request already texts them). Ships off; unreadable reads off.

Settings > My Work > Support Requests, set by the master account alone. ON means a vehicle request or issue goes straight to the directors as a My Inbox item, then a text through the Smart Comms situation sr_vehicle_request. Ships off; unreadable reads off.

Settings > My Work > Support Requests, set by the master account alone. ON means a payroll or pay-stub request goes straight to the payroll list as a My Inbox item, then a text through the Smart Comms situation sr_payroll_request. Ships off; unreadable reads off.

Settings > My Work > Support Requests, set by the master account alone. ON means an ADP - Update Information request is judged against its call: a home address read back and confirmed is applied on the platform and the directors are told (sr_adp_applied); a new e-mail or phone waits for one approval; anything else is refused as ADP only. Ships off; unreadable reads off.

Settings > My Work > Support Requests, set by the master account alone. ON means a vacation asked in My Calendar is filed into Scheduling's time-off flow (directors only, 7 days' notice) and shows in Support Requests and the directors' My Inbox; off keeps the Time Off app. Ships off; unreadable reads off.
